verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              पार्थिवेन विशेषेण किं कार्यमवशिष्यते। कथं रक्ष्यो जनपदः कथं जेयाश्च शत्रवः॥१॥
verses.english: Shuka said I have now understood that there are two kinds of creation, viz., one universal emanating from the (universal) Soul. The other consisting of the senses with their objects, originates from the power of the Understanding. This last transcends the other and is considered to be the foremost.

verses.sanskrit: कथं चारं प्रयुञ्जीत वर्णान्विश्वासयेत्कथम्। कथं भृत्यान्कथं दारान्कथं पुत्रांश्च भारत॥२॥
verses.english: I wish however, to once more hear of that path of righteousness which runs in this world, regulated by the virtue of Time and according to which all good men form their conduct.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              राजवृत्तं महाराज शृणुष्वावहितोऽखिलम्। यत्कार्यं पार्थिवेनादौ पार्थिवप्रकृतेन वा॥३॥
verses.english: In the Vedas there are both kinds of saying, do acts and avoid acts. How shall I succeed in determining which of the two is right? You should explain this clearly.

verses.sanskrit: आत्मा जेयः सदा राज्ञा ततो जेयाश्च शत्रवः। अजितात्मा नरपतिर्विजयेत कथं रिपून्॥४॥
verses.english: Having acquired through your instructions, a thorough knowledge of the course of conduct of human beings, having purified myself by the practice of only righteousness, and having cleansed my understanding, I shall, after renouncing my body, see the indestructible Soul.

verses.sanskrit: एतावानात्मविजयः पञ्चवर्गविनिग्रहः। जितेन्द्रियो नरपतिर्बाधितुं शक्नुयादरीन्॥५॥
verses.english: The course of conduct that was fist laid down by Brahman himself was duly followed by the wise and pious persons of yore viz., the great Rishis of ancient times.

verses.sanskrit: न्यसेत गुल्मान्दुर्गेषु सन्धौ च कुरुनन्दन। नगरोपवने चैव पुरोद्यानेषु चैव ह॥६॥
verses.english: The great Rishis conquer all the worlds by the practice of celebacy. Seeking all things which are good for himself, by fixing the mind the understanding, practising austerities, by living in forest and lying on fruits and roots, by treading on sacred spots, by practising universal benevolence, and by begging alms at the proper time from the huts of herinits when these become smokeless and the sound of the husking rod is hushed a person attains to Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: संस्थानेषु च सर्वेषु पुरेषु नगरेषु च। मध्ये च नरशार्दूल तथा राजनिवेशने॥७॥
प्रणिधींश्च ततः कुर्याज्जडान्धबधिराकृतीन्। पुंसः परीक्षितान्प्राज्ञान्क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमक्षयान्॥८॥
verses.english: Abstaining from flattery and from bowing your head to others, and avoiding both good and evil, live in the forest alone appeasing hunger by any means that presents itself before you.

verses.sanskrit: अमात्येषु च सर्वेषु मित्रेषु विविधेषु च। पुत्रेषु च महाराज प्रणिदध्यात्समाहितः॥९॥
verses.english: The saying of the Vedas are, in the opinion of the ordinary person, contradictory. Whether on severe ! this is authoritative or that is so, when there is this conflict, how can they be considered to be spiritual.

verses.sanskrit: पुरे जनपदे चैव तथा सामन्तराजसु। यथा न विद्युरन्योन्यं प्रणिधेयास्तथा हि ते॥१०॥
चारांश्च विद्यात्प्रहितान्पुरेण भरतर्षभ। आपणेषु विहारेषु समाजेषु च भिक्षुषु॥११॥
verses.english: I wish to hear this; how can both be considered as authoritative. How indeed, can liberation be obtained without violating the ordinance regarding the obligatory character of acts.

verses.sanskrit: आरामेषु तथोद्याने पण्डितानां समागमे। देशेषु चत्वरे चैव सभास्वावसथेषु च॥१२॥
एवं विचिनुयाद्राजा परचारं विचक्षणः। चारे हि विदिते पूर्वं हितं भवति पाण्डव॥१३॥
यदा तु हीनं नृपतिर्विद्यादात्मानमात्मना। अमात्यैः सह सम्मन्त्र्य कुर्यात्सन्धिं बलीयसा॥१४॥
अज्ञायमाने हीनत्वे सन्धिं कुर्यात्परेण वै। लिप्सुर्वा कंचिदेवार्थं त्वरमाणो विचक्षणः॥१५॥
गुणवन्तो महोत्साहा धर्मज्ञाः साधवश्च ये। सन्दधीत नृपस्तैश्च राष्ट्रं धर्मेण पालयन्॥१६॥
उच्छिद्यमानमात्मानं ज्ञात्वा राजा महामतिः। पूर्वापकारिणो हन्याल्लोकद्विष्टांश्च सर्वशः॥१७॥
यो नोपकर्तुं शक्नोति नोपकर्तुं महीपतिः। न शक्यरूपश्चोद्धर्तुमुपेक्ष्यस्तादृशो भवेत्॥१८॥
यात्रायां यदि विज्ञातमनाक्रन्दमनन्तरम्। व्यासक्तं च प्रमत्तं च दुर्बलं च विचक्षणः॥१९॥
verses.english: Having performed all acts, he should study, sitting at the feet of his preceptor, with anxious desire to learn. He should always behave with simplicity, avoid evil speech, and take lessons only when his preceptor asks him for it.

verses.sanskrit: यात्रामाज्ञापयेद्वीरः कल्यः पुष्टबलः सुखी। पूर्वं कृत्वा विधानं च यात्रायां नगरे तथा॥२०॥
न च वश्यो भवेदस्य नृपो यश्चातिवीर्यवान्। हीनश्च बलवीर्याभ्यां कर्षयंस्तत्परो वसेत्॥२१॥
राष्ट्रं च पीडयेत्तस्य शस्त्राग्निविषमूर्च्छनैः। अमात्यवल्लभानां च विवादांस्तस्य कारयेत्॥२२॥
वर्जनीयं सदा युद्धं राज्यकामेन धीमता। उपायैस्त्रिभिरादानमर्थस्याह बृहस्पतिः॥२३॥
सान्त्वेन तु प्रदानेन भेदेन च नराधिप। यदर्थं शक्नुयात्प्राप्तुं तेन तुष्येत पण्डितः॥२४॥
आददीत बलिं चापि प्रजाभ्यः कुरुनन्दन। स षड्भागमपि प्राज्ञस्तासामेवाभिगुप्तये॥२५॥
दशधर्मगतेभ्यो यद्वसु बह्वल्पमेव च। तदाददीत सहसा पौराणां रक्षणाय वै॥२६॥
verses.english: What scents or tastes the Brahmacharin may abstain from while actually leading a life of celebacy may be used by him after his return from the preceptor's house. This is according to the ordinance.

verses.sanskrit: यथा पुत्रास्तथा पौत्रा द्रष्टव्यास्ते न संशयः। भक्तिश्चैषां न कर्तव्या व्यवहारे प्रदर्शिते॥२७॥
verses.english: Whatever observances have been laid down in full for Brahmacharins should all be regularly practised by him. He should all be regularly practised by him. He should be always at the beck and call of his preceptor.

verses.sanskrit: श्रोतुं चैव न्यसेद्राजा प्राज्ञान्सर्वार्थदर्शिनः। व्यवहारेषु सततं तत्र राज्यं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥२८॥
verses.english: Having pleased his preceptor in this way to the best of his powers, the disciple should, from that mode of life, enter into the others and practise the duties of each.

verses.sanskrit: आकरे लवणे शुल्के तरे नागबले तथा। न्यसेदमात्यान्नृपतिः स्वाप्तान्वा पुरुषान्हितान्॥२९॥
verses.english: Having (thus) spent a fourth part of his life in the study of the Vedas, and observance of vows and fasts, and given the preceptor his fee, the disciple should, according to the ordinance, bidadicu and return home for becoming a house-holder.

verses.sanskrit: सम्यग्दण्डधरो नित्यं राजा धर्ममवाप्नुयात्। नृपस्य सततं दण्डः सम्यग्धर्मः प्रशस्यते॥३०॥
verses.english: Then, having married according to the ordinances, and having carefully established the domestic fire, he should, observing all the Vows and fasts, become a house-holder and pass the second period of life. the disciple should, according to the ordinance, bidadicu and return home for becoming a house-holder.

verses.sanskrit: वेदवेदाङ्गवित्प्राज्ञः सुतपस्वी नृपो भवेत्। दानशीलश्च सततं यज्ञशीलश्च भारत॥३१॥
verses.english: Then, having married according to the ordinances, and having carefully established the domestic fire, he should, observing all the Vows and fasts, become a house-holder and pass the second period of life.

verses.sanskrit: एते गुणाः समस्ताः स्युर्नृपस्य सततं स्थिराः। व्यवहारलोपे नृपतेः कुतः स्वर्गः कुतो यशः॥३२॥
verses.english: All these qualities should always be in a king. If the king fails to administer justice, he can neither acquire heaven nor fame.

verses.sanskrit: यदा तु पीडितो राजा भवेद्राजा बलीयसा। तदाभिसंश्रयेद्दुर्गं बुद्धिमान्पृथिवीपतिः॥३३॥
verses.english: If a king be attacked by a stronger one, the former, if intelligent, should seek refuge in a fort.

verses.sanskrit: विधानाऽक्रम्य मित्राणि विधानमुपकल्पयेत्। सामभेदान्विरोधार्थं विधानमुपकल्पयेत्॥३४॥
verses.english: Collecting his friends for consultation, he should devise proper means. Adopting the policy of conciliation and of creating dissensions, he should devise means for fighting with the assailants.

verses.sanskrit: घोषान्न्यसेत मार्गेषु ग्रामानुत्थापयेदपि। प्रवेशयेच्च तान्सर्वान् शाखानगरकेष्वपि॥३५॥
verses.english: He should place the inhabitants of the woods on the high roads, and, it, necessary, cause whole villages to be removed, removing all the inhabitants of minor towns or on the outskirts of great cities.

verses.sanskrit: ये गुप्ताश्चैव दुर्गाश्च देशास्तेषु प्रवेशयेत्। धनिनो बलमुख्यांश्च सान्त्वयित्वा पुनः पुनः॥३६॥
verses.english: Giving repeated assurances to his wealthy subjects and the principal officers of the army, he should make the dwellers of the open country to take refuge in well-protected forts.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याभिहारं कुर्याच्च स्वयमेव नराधिपः। असम्भवे प्रवेशस्य दहेद्दावाग्निना भृशम्॥३७॥
verses.english: He should deposit all sorts of grain in his forts. If that is impossible, he should destroy them completely by fire.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेत्रस्थेषु च सस्येषु शत्रोरुपजयेन्नरान्। विनाशयेद्वा तत्सर्वं बलेनाथ स्वकेन वा॥३८॥
verses.english: He should engage men for destroying the crops on the fields of the enemy. Failing to do this, he should destroy those crops to do this, he should destroy those crops by means of his own men.

verses.sanskrit: नदीमार्गेषु च तथा संक्रमानवसादयेत्। जलं विस्त्रावयेत्सर्वमविस्रव्यं च दूषयेत्॥३९॥
verses.english: He should destroying all the bridges over the rivers in his kingdom. He should draw out the waters of all the tanks in his territories, or, if incapable to do so, cause them to be poisoned.

verses.sanskrit: तदात्वेनायतीभिश्च निवसेद्भूम्यनन्तरम्। प्रतीघातं परस्याजौ मित्रकार्येऽप्युपस्थिते॥४०॥
verses.english: Disregarding the duty of protecting his friends, he should, considering present and future circumstances, seek the protection of another king who may happen to be the foe of his foe and who may be capable to fight with his enemy on the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्गाणां चाभितो राजा मूलच्छेदं प्रकारयेत्। सर्वेषां क्षुद्रवृक्षाणां चैत्यवृक्षान्विवर्जयेत्॥४१॥
verses.english: He should demolish all the minor forts in his kingdom. He should also cut down all the smaller trees except those called Chaitya.

verses.sanskrit: प्रवृद्धानां च वृक्षाणां शाखां प्रच्छेदयेत्तथा। चैत्यानां सर्वथा त्याज्यमपि पत्रस्य पातनम्॥४२॥
verses.english: He should cause the branches of all large threes to be cut off, but he should not touch the very leaves of Chaitya ones.

verses.sanskrit: प्रगण्डीः कारयेत्सम्यगाकाशजननीस्तदा। आपूरयेच्च परिखां स्थाणु-नक्र-झषाकुलाम्॥४३॥
verses.english: He should erect outer ramparts round his forts, and fill his trenches with water, putting pointed stakes at their bottom and filling them with crocodiles and sharks.

verses.sanskrit: संकटद्वारकाणि स्युरुच्छ्वासार्थं पुरस्य च। तेषां च द्वारवद्गुप्तिः कार्या सर्वात्मना भवेत्॥४४॥
verses.english: He should keep small outlets in his walls for firing guns from his fort, and carefully make arrangements for their defence like that of the greater gates.

verses.sanskrit: द्वारेषु च गुरूण्येव यन्त्राणि स्थापयेत्सदा। आरोपयेच्छतघ्नीश्च स्वाधीनानि च कारयेत्॥४५॥
verses.english: In all his gates he should place destructive engines. He should place on ramparts Shataghnis and other weapons.

verses.sanskrit: काष्ठानि चाभिहार्याणि तथा कूपांश्च खानयेत्। संशोधयेत्तथा कूपान् कृतपूर्वान् पयोऽर्थिभिः॥४६॥
verses.english: He should lay by wood for fuel and dig and repair wells for supply of water to the garrison.

verses.sanskrit: तृणच्छन्नानि वेश्मानि पङ्केनाथ प्रलेपयेत्। निर्हरेच्च तृणं मासि चैत्रे वह्निभयात्तथा॥४७॥
verses.english: He should have all houses made of grass and straw plastered over with mud, and if it is summer, he should, from fear of fire, collect in a safe place all the stores of grass and straw.

verses.sanskrit: नक्तमेव च भक्तानि पाचयेत नराधिपः। न दिवा ज्वालयेदग्निं वर्जयित्वाऽऽग्निहोत्रिकम्॥४८॥
verses.english: He should order all food to be cooked at night. No fire should be lighted during the day, except for the daily Homa.

verses.sanskrit: कर्मारारिष्टशालासु ज्वलेदग्निः सुरक्षितः। गृहाणि च प्रवेश्यान्तर्विधेयः स्याद्धुताशनः॥४९॥
verses.english: Particular care should be taken of the fires lighted in smitheries and lying-in chambers. Fires in the houses of the inhabitants should be well covered.

verses.sanskrit: महादण्डश्च तस्य स्याद्यस्याग्निर्वै दिवा भवेत्। प्रघोषयेदथैवं च रक्षणार्थं पुरस्य च॥५०॥
verses.english: For the better protection of the city, it should be announced that a person, lighting fires in the day time, will be sufficiently punished.

verses.sanskrit: भिक्षुकांश्चाक्रिकांश्चैव क्लीबोन्मत्तान्कुशीलवान्। बाह्यान् कुर्यान्नरश्रेष्ठ दोषाय स्युर्हि तेऽन्यथा॥५१॥
verses.english: During such times, all beggars, cartmen, eunuchs, lunatics, should, O foremost of men, be driven out of the town, for if they are allowed to remain, evil will come.

verses.sanskrit: चत्वरेष्वथ तीर्थेषु सभास्वावसथेषु च। यथार्थवर्णं प्रणिधिं कुर्यात्सर्वस्य पार्थिवः॥५२॥
verses.english: In places of public resort, in Tirthas, in assemblies and in the houses of the citizens, the king should keep capable spies.

verses.sanskrit: विशालान् राजमार्गांश्च कारयीत नराधिपः। प्रपाश्च विपणांश्चैव यथोद्देशं समाविशेत्॥५३॥
verses.english: The king should have wide roads constructed, and open up shops, and places for the distribution of water, at proper stations.

verses.sanskrit: भाण्डागारायुधागारान्योधागारांश्च सर्वशः। अश्वागारान्गजागारान्बलाधिकरणानि च॥५४॥
verses.english: Shops of necessary articles, arsenals, camps and quarters for soldiers, stables for horses and elephants, encampments, of soldiers, trenches, streets and lanes, houses and pleasure gardens should be so made that their situations may not be known to others, O Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: परिखाश्चैव कौरव्य प्रतोलीर्निष्कुटानि च। न जात्वन्यः प्रपश्येत गुह्यमेतद्युधिष्ठिर॥५५॥
अर्थसंनिचयं कुर्याद्राजा परबलार्दितः। तैलं वसा मधु घृतमौषधानि च सर्वशः॥५६॥
verses.english: A king, who is attacked by a hostile army, should collect wealth, and store oil and fat and honey, and clarified butter, and medicines of all sorts,

verses.sanskrit: अङ्गारकुशमुञ्जानां पलाशशरवर्णिनाम्। यवसेन्धनादिग्धानां कारयीत च संचयान्॥५७॥
verses.english: And charcoal and munja grass, leaves, arrows, scribes and draftsmen, grass, fuel, poisoned arrows, weapons of all sorts such as darts, swords, lances and others, The king should store such articles.

verses.sanskrit: आयुधानां च सर्वेषां शक्त्यृष्टिप्रासवर्मणाम्। संचयानेवमादीनां कारयीत नराधिपः॥५८॥
औषधानि च सर्वाणि मूलानि च फलानि च। चतुर्विधांश्च वैद्यान्वै संगृह्णीयाद्विशेषतः॥५९॥
verses.english: He should especially keep ready various drugs, roots and fruits, the four kinds of physicians, actors and dancers, athletes, and persons capable of assuming various disguises. He should adorn his capital and please all his subjects.

verses.sanskrit: नटांश्च नर्तकांश्चैव मल्लान्मायाविनस्तथा। शोभयेयुः पुरवरं मोदयेयुश्च सर्वशः॥६०॥
यतः शङ्का भवेच्चापि भृत्यतोऽथापि मन्त्रितः। पौरेभ्यो नृपतेर्वापि स्वाधीनान्कारयीत तान्॥६१॥
verses.english: The king should speedily subjugate such persons as may cause fear, be they his servants or counsellors or citizens or neighbouring kings.

verses.sanskrit: कृते कर्मणि राजेन्द्र पूजयेद्धनसञ्चयैः। दानेन च यथार्हेण सान्त्वेन विविधेन च॥६२॥
verses.english: Whenever any of his work is done the king should reward those who have helped in its accomplishment with wealth and other becoming presents and grateful speeches.

verses.sanskrit: निर्वेदयित्वा तु परं हत्वा वा कुरुनन्दन। ततोऽनृणो भवेद्राजा यथा शास्त्रे निदर्शितम्॥६३॥
verses.english: It has been laid down in the scriptures, O delighter of the Kurus, that a king satisfies his debt when he defeats his foe or kills him at once.

verses.sanskrit: राज्ञा सप्तैव रक्ष्याणि तानि चैव निबोध मे। आत्माऽमात्याश्च कोशाश्च दण्डो मित्राणि चैव हि॥६४॥
verses.english: A king should take care of seven things. Listen to me as I name them. They are his own self, his ministers, his treasury, his servants for inflicting punishments, his friends, his provinces, and his capital. He should carefully protect his kingdom consisting of these seven limbs.

verses.sanskrit: तथा जनपदाश्चैव पुरं च कुरुनन्दन। एतत्सप्तात्मकं राज्यं परिपाल्यं प्रयत्नतः॥६५॥
षाड्गुण्यं च त्रिवर्गं च त्रिवर्गपरमं तथा। यो वेत्ति पुरुषव्याघ्र स भुंक्ते पृथिवीमिमाम्॥६६॥
verses.english: That king, O foremost of man, who is conversant with the collection of six and three objects, and the high collection of three, gains the sovereignty of the whole Earth.

verses.sanskrit: षाड्गुण्यमिति यत्प्रोक्तं तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर। सन्धानासनमित्येव यात्रासन्धानमेव च॥६७॥
verses.english: Hear, O Yudhishthira, what is called the aggregate of six. They are ruling peacefully after making a treaty (with the foe), marching to battle, creating disunion among the enemy, concentration of army for filling the enemy with fear, preparation for war with readiness for peace, and alliances with others.

verses.sanskrit: विगृह्यासनमित्येव यात्रां सम्परिगृह्य च। द्वैधीभावस्तथाऽन्येषां संश्रयोऽथ परस्य च॥६८॥
त्रिवर्गश्चापि यः प्रोक्तस्तमिहैकमनाः शृणु। क्षयः स्थानं च वृद्धिश्च त्रिवर्गः परमस्तथा॥६९॥
verses.english: Listen now with attention to what are the triple objects. They are decrease, maintenance of what is, and growth. The great three fold objects consist of religion, Profit and Pleasure. These should be followed judiciously. By the help of religion a king succeeds in ruling the Earth for ever.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च सेवितव्योऽथ कालतः। धर्मेण च महीपालश्चिरं पालयते महीम्॥७०॥
अस्मिन्नर्थे च श्लोकौ द्वौ गीतावङ्गिरसा स्वयम्। यादवीपुत्र भद्रं ते तावपि श्रोतुमर्हसि॥७१॥
verses.english: Regarding this matter, Angirasa's son Brihaspati himself has recited two verses. Blessed be you, O son of Devaki, you should

verses.sanskrit: कृत्वा सर्वाणि कार्याणि सम्यक्सम्पाल्य मेदिनीम्। पालयित्वा तथा पौरान्परत्र सुखमेधते॥७२॥
verses.english: 'Having satisfied all his duties and having protected the Earth, and having also protected the cities, a king enjoys great happiness in heaven.

verses.sanskrit: किं तस्य तपसा राज्ञः किं च तस्याध्वरैरपि। सुपालितप्रजो यः स्यात्सर्वधर्मविदेव सः॥७३॥
verses.english: Of what use are penances to that king, and what need has he of sacrifices who protects his people properly? Such a king should be known as one conversant with every virtue.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              दण्डनीतिश्च राजा च समस्तौ तावुभावपि। कस्य किं कुर्वतः सिद्ध्येत्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥७४॥

भीष्म उवाच।
              महाभाग्यं दण्डनीत्याः सिद्धैः शब्दैः सहेतुकैः। शृणु मे शंसतो राजन् यथावदिह भारत॥७५॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Listen to me, O king, as I describe, O Bharata, the great virtues of the science of punishment in weighty and sacred words.

verses.sanskrit: दण्डनीतिः स्वधर्मेभ्यश्चातुर्वर्ण्यं नियच्छति। प्रयुक्ता स्वामिना सम्यगधर्मेभ्यो नियच्छति॥७६॥
verses.english: The science of punishment compels all men to satisfy the duties of their respective orders. Properly administered, it compels people to perform virtuous acts.

verses.sanskrit: चातुर्वर्ण्ये स्वकर्मस्थे मर्यादानामसंकरे। दण्डनीतिकृते क्षेमे प्रजानामकुतोभये॥७७॥
verses.english: When the four orders perform their respective duties, when all healthy restrictions are kept up, when peace and happiness emanate from the science of punishment when the people are shorn of all fear, and the three higher orders try according to their respective duties, to preserve harmony people become truly happy at such times.

verses.sanskrit: स्वाम्ये प्रयत्नं कुर्वन्ति त्रयो वर्णा यथाविधि। तस्मादेव मनुष्याणां सुखं विद्धि समाहितम्॥७८॥
कालो वा कारणं राज्ञो राजा वा कालकारणम्। इति ते संशयो मा भूद्राजा कालस्य कारणम्॥७९॥
verses.english: You should not doubt whether it is the king that makes the age, or, it is the age that makes the king; the truth is that the king makes the age.

verses.sanskrit: दण्डनीत्यां यदा राजा सम्यक्कार्त्स्न्येन वर्तते। तदा कृतयुगं नाम कालसृष्टं प्रवर्तते॥८०॥
verses.english: When the king rules depending entirely on the science of punishment the foremost of ages called Krita is then said flourish.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कृतयुगे धर्मो नाधर्मो विद्यते क्वचित्। सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां नाधर्मे रमते मनः॥८१॥
verses.english: Righteousness prevails in the Krita age. Nothing unrighteous exists then; the four orders are not inclined to take any pleasure in unrighteousness.

verses.sanskrit: योगक्षेमाः प्रवर्तन्ते प्रजानां नात्र संशयः। वैदिकानि च सर्वाणि भवन्त्यपि गुणान्युत॥८२॥
verses.english: Forsooth, all men succeed in acquiring the objects they seek and preserving those that have been acquired. All the Vedic rites yield merit.

verses.sanskrit: ऋतवश्च सुखाः सर्वे भवन्त्युत निरामयाः। प्रसीदन्ति नराणां च स्वरवर्णमनांसि च॥८३॥
verses.english: All the seasons are delightful and free from evil. The voice pronunciation, and minds of all men became clear and delightful.

verses.sanskrit: व्याधयो न भवन्त्यत्र नाल्पायुर्दृश्यते नरः। विधवा न भवन्त्यत्र कृपणो न तु जायते॥८४॥
verses.english: Ailments disappear and all men enjoy long lives. Wives do not become widows, and no person becomes a miser.

verses.sanskrit: अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी भवन्त्योषधयस्तथा। त्वक्पत्रफलमूलानि वीर्यवन्ति भवन्ति च॥८५॥
verses.english: The Earth yield crops without being cultivated and herbs and plants grow abundantly. Barks, leaves, fruits, and roots, become strong and profuse.

verses.sanskrit: नाधर्मो विद्यते तत्र धर्म एव तु केवलम्। इति कार्तयुगानेतान्धर्मान्विद्धि युधिष्ठिर॥८६॥
verses.english: No unrighteousness is seen. Nothing but righteousness exists. These are the characteristics, O Yudhishthira, of the Krita.

verses.sanskrit: दण्डनीत्यां यदा राजा त्रीनंशाननुवर्तते। चतुर्थमंशमुत्सृज्य तदा त्रेता प्रवर्तते॥८७॥
verses.english: When the king depends upon only three of the four parts of the science of punishment leaving out a fourth, the age called Treta sets in.

verses.sanskrit: अशुभस्य चतुर्थांशस्त्रीनंशाननुवर्तते। कृष्टपच्यैव पृथिवी भवन्त्योषधयस्तथा॥८८॥
verses.english: A fourth part of unrighteousness sets in by the observance of the great science by threefourths. The Earth gives crops but waits for cultivation; the herbs and plants grow by cultivation.

verses.sanskrit: अर्धं त्यक्त्वा यदा राजा नीत्यर्धमनुवर्तते। ततस्तु द्वापरं नाम स कालः सम्प्रवर्तते॥८९॥
verses.english: When the king follows the great science by only a half, leaving out the other half, then the age that sets in is called Dvapara.

verses.sanskrit: अशुभस्य यदा त्वर्धं द्वावंशावनुवर्तते। कृष्टपच्यैव पृथिवी भवत्यर्धफला तथा॥९०॥
verses.english: A half of unrighteousness follows the observance of the great science by half. The Earth yields crops by half and that even by tillage.

verses.sanskrit: दण्डनीतिं परित्यज्य यदा कार्त्स्येन भूमिपः। प्रजाः क्लिश्नात्ययोगेन प्रवर्तेत तदा कलिः॥९१॥
verses.english: When the king, leaving aside the great science altogether, oppresses his subjects by all manner and means the age that sets in is called Kali.

verses.sanskrit: कलावधर्मो भूयिष्ठं धर्मो भवति न क्वचित्। सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां स्वधर्माच्च्यवते मनः॥९२॥
verses.english: During the age called Kali, unrighteousness assumes the full proportion and nothing of righteousness is seen. The hearts of men of all the orders, are disinclined to their respective duties.

verses.sanskrit: शूद्रा भैक्षेण जीवन्ति ब्राह्मणाः परिचर्यया। योगक्षेमस्य नाशश्च वर्तते वर्णसंकरः॥९३॥
verses.english: Shudras live by adopting lives of mendicancy, and Brahmanas live by serving others. Men cannot acquire the objects they seek and preserve those already acquired. Intermixture of the four castes takes place.

verses.sanskrit: वैदिकानि च कर्माणि भवन्ति विगुणान्युत। ऋतवो न सुखाः सर्वे भवन्त्यामयिनस्तथा॥९४॥
verses.english: Vedic rites fail to yield fruits. All the seasons eases to the delightful and visited by evils.

verses.sanskrit: ह्रसन्ति च मनुष्याणां स्वरवर्णमनांस्युत। व्याधयश्च भवन्त्यत्र म्रियन्ते च गतायुषः॥९५॥
verses.english: The voice, pronunciation, and minds of men lose power. Diseases appear, and men die untimely.

verses.sanskrit: विधवाश्च भवन्त्यत्र नृशंसा जायते प्रजा। क्वचिद्वर्षति पर्जन्यः क्वचित्सस्यं प्ररोहति॥९६॥
verses.english: Wives become widows, and many cruel men appear; the clouds do not rain in seasons and crops fail.

verses.sanskrit: रसाः सर्वे क्षयं यान्ति यदा नेच्छति भूमिपः। प्रजाः संरक्षितुं सम्यग्दण्डनीतिसमाहितः॥९७॥
verses.english: All kinds of moisture also fail, when the king does not, by duly following the great science, protect the subjects.

verses.sanskrit: राजा कृतयुगस्रष्टा त्रेताया द्वापरस्य च। युगस्य च चतुर्थस्य राजा भवति कारणम्॥९८॥
verses.english: The king is the creator of the Krita age, of the Treta, and of the Dvapara. The king is the creator of the fourth age (called Kali).

verses.sanskrit: कृतस्य करणाद्राजा स्वर्गमत्यन्तमश्नुते। त्रेतायाः करणाद्राजा स्वर्गं नात्यन्तमश्नुते॥९९॥
verses.english: If he creates the Krita age, he acquires eternal heaven. If he creates the Treta age, he acquires heaven for a limited period.

verses.sanskrit: प्रवर्तनाद्द्वापरस्य यथाभागमुपाश्नुते। कलेः प्रवर्तनाद्राजा पापमत्यन्तमश्नुते॥१००॥
verses.english: If he creates the Dvapara, he attains to blessedness in heaven in proportion to his merits. By creating the Kali age, the king incurs a heavy sin.

verses.sanskrit: ततो वसति दुष्कर्मा नरके शाश्वतीः समाः। प्रजानां कल्मषे मग्नोऽकीर्तिं पापं च विन्दति॥१०१॥
verses.english: Sullied by wickedness, he suffers in hell for numberless years, for being drowned in the sins of his subjects, he incurs great sin and infamy himself.

verses.sanskrit: दण्डनीतिं पुरस्कृत्य विजानन्क्षत्रियः सदा। अनवाप्तं च लिप्सेत लब्धं च परिपालयेत्॥१०२॥
verses.english: Following the great science the learned Kshatriya should try to acquire those objects which he seeks and protect those which he has already acquired.

verses.sanskrit: लोकस्य सीमन्तकरी मर्यादा लोकभाविनी। सम्यङ्नीता दण्डनीतिर्यथा माता यथा पिता॥१०३॥
verses.english: The science of punishment, which establishes all men in the observance of their respective duties, which is the basis of all healthy distinctions, and which truly keeps up the world and sets it agoing if properly administered, protects all men like parents protecting their children.

verses.sanskrit: यस्यां भवन्ति भूतानि तद्विद्धि मनुजर्षभ। एष एव परो धर्मो यद्राजा दण्डनीतिमान्॥१०४॥
verses.english: Know, O foremost of men, that the very lives of creatures depend upon it. The greatest merit of a king consists in his acquaintance with the science of punishment and administering it properly.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्कौरव्य धर्मेण प्रजाः पालय नीतिमान्। एवंवृत्तः प्रजा रक्षन्स्वर्गं जेतासि दुर्जयम्॥१०५॥
verses.english: Therefore, O you of Kuru's race, protect your subjects righteously, with the help of that great science. By protecting your subjects and adopting such a conduct, you will, forsooth, attain to such blessedness in heaven which cannot be easily acquired.
